mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving up S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If forward returns are not higher during easing periods, or correlation is insignificant.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate suggests economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive when unemployment rises beyond the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate exceeds 2% and unemployment is below 5%, it may indicate a specific policy stance affecting market returns positively over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns do not follow the expected direction when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are negative when housing starts grow.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production suggests strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns do not correlate positively with industrial production growth.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are negative when retail sales grow.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If returns do not correlate with employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising GDP and housing starts indicates strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% and HOUST increases > 5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If returns do not follow when both conditions are met.
